description: Reviewed matching upper and lower bounds. Each certificate identifies the tight quantity, its parameter domain, primary sources and explicit graph/problem/model applications. Tightness is independent of SOTA ranking. It is not inferred from the current catalog, from a shared round regime, from approximation-scheme limits, or automatically through reductions and graph inclusions. Exact coefficients, asymptotic orders and minimum-round thresholds remain distinct.

certificates.parameterDomain: Deterministic n-independent locality; integral optimum.
certificates.statement: The approximation ratio is exactly tight; the absolute round count is not certified.

upper.title: Bonamy–Cook–Groenland–Wesolek
upper.statement: Ratio 5 is achieved in universally constant anonymous rounds.

lower.title: Bonamy–Cook–Groenland–Wesolek
lower.statement: Every ratio below 5 is impossible in deterministic LOCAL with n-independent locality.

certificates.parameterDomain: Integral benchmark; fixed genus when relevant.
certificates.statement: Ratio 7 is tight, including the stated fixed-surface upper bound.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: Ratio 7: universal rounds on planar graphs; genus-dependent rounds on fixed surfaces.

lower.title: Hilke–Lenzen–Suomela
lower.statement: Deterministic local planar approximation below 7 is impossible.

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds · joint n and ε dependence
certificates.parameterDomain: log(n)/n < ε < 1; deterministic algorithms.
certificates.statement: The round complexity is Θ(log* n / ε).

upper.title: Faour–Kuhn
upper.statement: The upper bound holds for maximum-weight independent set on unrooted trees in CONGEST.

lower.title: Faour–Kuhn
lower.statement: The matching lower bound holds for unweighted oriented paths even in LOCAL.

certificates.parameterDomain: k ≥ 1; fixed k-hop expansion bound and girth ≥ 4k+3; connected input.
certificates.statement: The dependence k + f(k)^(k/(k+1)) is tight up to multiplicative constants.

upper.title: Lenzen–Wenning
upper.statement: This approximation order is achieved in 3k rounds with small anonymous messages.

lower.title: Lenzen–Wenning
lower.statement: No deterministic n-independent algorithm improves the approximation order, even with identifiers.

certificates.scopeLabel: Minimum k rounds · factor independent of Δ
certificates.parameterDomain: k ≥ 2; fixed expansion bound at least 1; classes include trees of arbitrarily large degree.
certificates.statement: Exactly k rounds are sufficient and necessary for a factor independent of Δ; the upper coefficient is not certified optimal.

upper.title: Lenzen–Wenning
upper.statement: A factor 2k f(k)+1 is achieved in exactly k rounds.

lower.title: Lenzen–Wenning
lower.statement: At k−1 rounds a factor smaller than Δ is impossible already on trees.

certificates.parameterDomain: Fixed α ≥ 2; known Δ for the upper; polylogarithmic approximation factors in Δ.
certificates.statement: The degree-dependent round order is Θ(log Δ / log log Δ), not the approximation coefficient.

upper.title: Alipour–Farokhnejad
upper.statement: A deterministic CONGEST upper bound attains this round order with O(α log Δ / log log Δ) approximation and one-bit messages.

lower.title: Dory–Ghaffari–Ilchi
lower.statement: The matching lower bound for constant or polylogarithmic approximation already holds at arboricity 2, even in LOCAL.

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds in n · fixed ρ, b, ε
certificates.parameterDomain: ρ ≥ 1; fixed positive integer b; fixed 0 < ε < 1/4; unit costs for MDS.
certificates.statement: The n-dependence is Θ(log* n); parameter dependence is not certified.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: Integral local covering admits the upper bound; unit-cost MDS is a special case.

lower.title: ASW26
lower.statement: The lower bound already holds for deterministic MDS on cycles.

certificates.parameterDomain: Integer a ≥ 1; every minor has density at most a; lower path-power radius r=a.
certificates.statement: The coefficient is tight on these density classes; round dependence on a is not certified.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: The upper coefficient is 2a+1 against fractional OPT.

lower.title: Amiri–Siebertz
lower.statement: Path powers of radius r have minor density at most r and exclude every coefficient below 2r+1.

certificates.parameterDomain: Integer t ≥ 1; identifiers in {1,…,n}; use a=t in the minor-density upper bound.
certificates.statement: The endpoint-leaf lower bound is matched by the density-class upper bound.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: At a=t the upper coefficient is 2t+1.

lower.title: Picavet thesis
lower.statement: For identifiers in {1,…,n} and every function f, an f(t)-round deterministic algorithm cannot beat 2t+1 on the stated path-power family.

certificates.parameterDomain: Deterministic n-independent locality; integral benchmark.
certificates.statement: The coefficient 5 is tight; runtime constants are not certified.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: Ratio 5 is achieved against fractional OPT.

lower.title: ASW26
lower.statement: Square-grid witnesses exclude every ratio below 5, even against integral OPT.

certificates.parameterDomain: Δ ≥ 2; deterministic locality may depend on Δ but is independent of n.
certificates.statement: The degree-dependent approximation coefficient is exactly tight; runtime dependence on Δ is not certified.

upper.title: Göös–Hirvonen–Suomela
upper.statement: The theorem explicitly states a matching deterministic local upper bound.

lower.title: Göös–Hirvonen–Suomela
lower.statement: The same coefficient is necessary on connected maximum-degree-Δ graphs, including algorithms with identifiers.

certificates.parameterDomain: Integer a ≥ 1; isolate-free inputs; fractional total-domination benchmark.
certificates.statement: Coefficient 2a is tight against fractional OPT; neither integral-benchmark tightness for a>1 nor optimal runtime is claimed.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: The upper coefficient is 2a.

lower.title: ASW26
lower.statement: Treewidth-a witnesses force coefficient 2a against fractional OPT.

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds in n · fixed nonplanar H, ε
certificates.parameterDomain: Fixed nonplanar excluded minor H and fixed 0 < ε < 1/2.
certificates.statement: The n-dependence is Θ(log* n); the additive inverse-accuracy term is not certified tight.

upper.title: Chang
upper.statement: A deterministic CONGEST upper bound gives this n-dependence.

lower.title: Chang
lower.statement: Paths and cycles require Ω(log* n) for fixed ε, already in LOCAL.

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds in n · fixed α and ε
certificates.parameterDomain: Fixed α ≥ 1 and fixed 0 < ε < 1/2.
certificates.statement: The n-dependence is Θ(log* n); joint α and ε dependence is not certified.

upper.title: Czygrinow–Hańćkowiak–Wawrzyniak
upper.statement: For fixed arboricity and accuracy, the deterministic LOCAL scheme uses O(log* n) rounds.

lower.title: Chang
lower.statement: The matching problem inherits the Ω(log* n) lower bound on paths and cycles.

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds in n · fixed ε and expansion
certificates.parameterDomain: Fixed 0 < ε < 1/2 and sub-logarithmic expansion bounds; unit capacities are allowed.
certificates.statement: The worst-case n-dependence is Θ(log* n); accuracy, expansion and capacity dependence are not certified.

upper.title: Czygrinow–Hańćkowiak–Witkowski
upper.statement: The f-matching scheme uses O(log* n) rounds for fixed parameters.

lower.title: Chang
lower.statement: Unit capacities recover ordinary matching, whose path and cycle lower bound is Ω(log* n).

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds in n · fixed ε, L and expansion
certificates.parameterDomain: Fixed 0 < ε < 1/2, Lipschitz bound L and sub-logarithmic expansion bounds; unit capacities are allowed.
certificates.statement: The worst-case n-dependence is Θ(log* n); the other parameter dependencies are not certified.

upper.title: Czygrinow–Hańćkowiak–Witkowski
upper.statement: The b-matching scheme uses O(log* n) rounds for fixed parameters.

lower.title: Chang
lower.statement: The unit-capacity case is ordinary matching and satisfies the Lipschitz promise; its path and cycle lower bound applies.

certificates.parameterDomain: Unweighted inputs; initial own-degree knowledge for the one-round construction.
certificates.statement: Ratio 3 is tight; this does not certify that all optimal-ratio algorithms need one round.

upper.title: Dory–Ghaffari–Ilchi
upper.location: Appendix A, Observation A.1; elementary extension in the atlas
upper.statement: The documented forest rule has ratio 3. The explicit atlas proof extends it to pseudoforests.

lower.title: ASW26
lower.statement: Paths rule out every coefficient below 3.

certificates.parameterDomain: Deterministic anonymous port numbering; positive integer weights; fixed degree and weight range for locality.
certificates.statement: The approximation ratio is exactly tight in this reviewed anonymous setting; runtime dependence on Δ and W is not certified.

upper.title: Åstrand–Suomela
upper.statement: The algorithm gives a weighted vertex cover of factor 2.

lower.title: Göös–Hirvonen–Suomela
lower.statement: No deterministic local algorithm improves factor 2, even with identifiers; this includes the anonymous model.

certificates.parameterDomain: Unweighted regular graphs of positive degree; zero-round algorithm.
certificates.statement: Ratio 2 is tight over this family, using the cycle subclass as a lower-bound witness.

upper.title: Bonamy–Gavoille–Picavet–Wesolek
upper.statement: Selecting every vertex gives factor 2 without communication.

lower.title: Göös–Hirvonen–Suomela
lower.location: Section 1.4, vertex-cover approximability and cycle lower bound
lower.statement: A factor below 2 on cycles would yield a nontrivial independent set in constant time; cycles are regular.

certificates.parameterDomain: k ∈ {3,4,5,6}; outside-solution k-domination on planar graphs; deterministic n-independent locality.
certificates.statement: For these four values of k, the zero-round approximation coefficient is exactly tight.

upper.title: Czygrinow–Hańćkowiak–Szymańska–Wawrzyniak–Witkowski
upper.statement: Selecting all vertices without communication gives ratio k/(k−2).

lower.title: Czygrinow–Hańćkowiak–Szymańska–Wawrzyniak–Witkowski
lower.statement: The matching lower bound allows identifiers and certifies k=3,4,5,6 only.

certificates.parameterDomain: k=r>1, r=o(log* n), fixed accuracy gap ε>0; cycles of length at least 4r+3; O(r) rounds.
certificates.statement: On this cycle specialization the coefficient 2r+1 is tight within O(r) rounds.

upper.title: Lenzen–Wenning
upper.statement: Every cycle has k-hop expansion bound 1; the k-round ratio 2k f(k)+1 specializes to 2r+1.

lower.title: Amiri–Wiederhake
lower.statement: In O(r) deterministic LOCAL rounds, ratio 2r+1−ε is impossible for the stated r and cycle lengths.
